heroLead: Brilliant is a small Ohio River community in Jefferson County, close enough to the West Virginia line that some families here hold minerals on both sides of the river.
intro: If your family's landholding history runs on both sides of the Ohio River near Brilliant, it's worth being precise about which parcels are actually in Ohio and subject to Ohio's mineral and recording laws, since West Virginia's rules on things like the dormant mineral doctrine differ from Ohio's. We only work Ohio-side interests here, but it's a distinction worth getting right before you go looking for records.
For Ohio-side tracts, Brilliant sits on the flank of the Utica play, and development in the immediate area has been lighter than in the core counties further south.

sections.heading: Confirming which state your tract is in
paragraphs: This sounds obvious, but river-adjacent land near Brilliant can have a confusing history if a family has held parcels on both banks over multiple generations. Jefferson County, Ohio deed records only cover Ohio-side land, recorded at the courthouse in Steubenville. If your paperwork references a different county name or state, you may be dealing with a separate parcel governed by different law entirely.

sections.heading: What flank position means for your offer
paragraphs: Unleased acreage near Brilliant is generally priced with more weight on the lower density of nearby wells compared to core counties like Belmont or Harrison. A tract with an existing lease or production history is a different conversation, priced against those actual results rather than proximity to the broader play.

sections.heading: Old river-town deeds and mineral severance
paragraphs: Because Brilliant has been settled for a long time as a river and rail community, some tracts here carry mineral severances that predate the current shale era by decades. A full title search will show whether and when that happened, and whether the interest has stayed active or gone quiet long enough to raise a dormant mineral question under ORC 5301.56.

faqs.question: My family owns land on both sides of the Ohio River near Brilliant. Does that complicate things?
faqs.answer: It can, since Ohio and West Virginia have different mineral rights laws. We only handle Ohio-side interests, so confirming which state your specific parcel sits in is an important first step.

faqs.question: Is Brilliant likely to see more Utica drilling?
faqs.answer: It's flank ground with lighter development than counties further south, which is factored honestly into how unleased acreage is priced.

faqs.question: How do I check if my interest has gone dormant?
faqs.answer: A search of the Jefferson County Recorder's index for any abandonment notice filed against your legal description will show if a dormant mineral claim is pending.
